cases.explain: The preposition 'с' (with) governs the instrumental case to show association.
The preposition 'на' (at) with the accusative case shows the object of attention.

cases.sentence: Что за удел мне от ___ свыше.
cases.explain: The preposition 'от' (from) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Пусть Бог меня взвесит на верных ___.
cases.explain: The preposition 'на' (on) with the prepositional case indicates location.
The preposition 'в' (in) with location governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Если один я съедал свой хлеб, сиротою им не делясь, я с юности растил его как ___.
cases.explain: The predicate after 'растил как' (brought up like) takes the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Если я видел гибнувшего нагим и нищего без ___.
cases.explain: The preposition 'без' (without) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Если рад я был гибели моего ___ ликовал, когда он попадал в беду.
cases.explain: The genitive case follows certain verbs expressing emotion like 'рад' (glad about).

reading.ru: Договор заключил я с моими глазами, чтобы мне не заглядываться на девушек.
reading.question: What covenant did Job make with his eyes?
options: Not to look lustfully at young women
reading.correct: Not to look lustfully at young women
reading.explain: The text explicitly states Job made a covenant with his eyes not to look lustfully at young women.

reading.ru: Не грешником ли беда суждена и гибель творящим зло?
reading.question: What is Job asking about the punishment of evil-doers?
options: Is calamity not appointed to the wicked and disaster to workers of iniquity?
reading.correct: Is calamity not appointed to the wicked and disaster to workers of iniquity?
reading.explain: Job poses a rhetorical question about whether calamity is appointed to the unrighteous and destruction to those who do evil.

reading.ru: Я боялся бед от Бога, и страшась его величия я не смог бы такого сделать.
reading.question: Why did Job fear doing evil?
options: Because of God's power and majesty
reading.correct: Because of God's power and majesty
reading.explain: Job explicitly says he feared God and was in awe of His majesty, which prevented him from committing such sins.

reading.ru: Если бы я на золото понадеялся и сказал бы сокровищу ты опора моя.
reading.question: What would Job have been guilty of if he had trusted in riches?
options: Putting his hope in treasure instead of God
reading.correct: Putting his hope in treasure instead of God
reading.explain: Job indicates that trusting in gold and calling treasure his confidence would be placing his hope in material wealth instead of God.

reading.ru: Если в шатре моем не говорили, насытится бы нам его мясом, но и странник не ночевал на улице, ведь мои двери отворялись прохожему.
reading.question: What does this passage tell us about Job's hospitality?
options: He invited everyone to share his meat and opened his doors to travelers
He was stingy with his food
reading.correct: He invited everyone to share his meat and opened his doors to travelers
reading.explain: The text indicates that the men of his household would never want for his meat, and strangers never slept outside because Job opened his doors to travelers.

reading.ru: Если я скрывал свой грех, как Адам, в сердце своем прятал вину, из-за страха перед толпой.
reading.question: What was Job not guilty of according to this passage?
options: Hiding sin out of fear of others
reading.correct: Hiding sin out of fear of others
reading.explain: Job is saying he was not guilty of the sin of hiding his transgressions in his heart or concealing his guilt due to fear of the crowd, as Adam did.
